description: Mailchimp offers a Marketing API for campaigns and a Transactional API (Mandrill) for event-driven email.
auth_notes: Marketing API accepts an API key or OAuth 2 token, sent via HTTP Basic or Bearer header. Transactional authentication in sources covers sending-domain verification only.
gate_detail: An API key for your own account is the fastest way to start; OAuth 2 is needed for third-party installs. Plan requirements and sandbox are not stated in the sources.
api_scope: Marketing API follows REST conventions on api.mailchimp.com/3.0 with OpenAPI descriptions and official client libraries; Transactional sends messages via API or SMTP.
mcp_notes: Official docs-search MCP server, not account access; a separate Transactional MCP guide exists. Agents act on accounts via API or skills.
blocker_detail: No approval or payment gate stated; OAuth 2 needed only for third-party integrations.

evidence.quote: An API key authenticates against the account that created it.
You can use either HTTP Basic Authentication or Bearer Authentication.
OAuth 2 authenticates against an account belonging to someone else.
The Marketing API generally follows REST conventions, with some deviations.
This searches documentation, not your Mailchimp account.
Mailchimp Transactional (formerly Mandrill) sends targeted and event-driven messages via the API or SMTP

uncertainties: Free vs paid plan requirement for API access is not stated.
Webhooks and sandbox are not covered in the visible sources.
Transactional API key mechanics are not shown.
